issues.title: [Feedback]: v0.32.0rc1 Release Feedback
issues.body:
# vLLM Ascend v0.32.0rc1 Release Feedback

We are preparing to release **vLLM Ascend v0.32.0rc1**, aligned with upstream **vLLM v0.32.0**.

This release candidate focuses on expanded model support, Model Runner V2 capabilities, context parallelism, speculative decoding, KV Cache management, and inference performance optimizations on Ascend hardware.

The final model and hardware support scope will be determined based on functional validation and the official release test report. Model and hardware combinations not listed in the final validated scope are not included in the release support claim.

## What's New

- **DeepSeek V4.1 Support and Optimizations:** Enhanced DeepSeek V4.1 inference with `torch.compile` acceleration, encoder/decoder SWA bounded replay, and improved execution across model runners.

- **Context Parallelism:** Expanded PCP and DCP capabilities, including GQA PCP-DCP stacking, graph execution for sharded decode requests, and DeepSeek V4.1 SWA bounded replay with PCP and DP.

- **Model Runner V2 and Speculative Decoding:** Enhanced MRV2 with draft-model speculative decoding, block verification, Gemma4 MTP, MultiModuleMTPSpeculator, N-gram speculative decoding, and PCP-aware speculative sampling.

- **Qwen3.8 Flash Next:** Added Qwen3.8 Flash Next support, including Pipeline Parallelism, Sequence Parallelism, QSA pooling with AscendStore, and prefill attention optimizations.

- **GLM Model Support and Optimizations:** Enhanced GLM-5.3-Flash with PCP, `torch.compile` for the backbone and MTP, CANN pooled indexing, and static kernel compilation. Added GLM KDA RecoverSSM framework integration, Triton operators, and prefix caching support.

- **KV Cache Quantization and Attention:** Extended C8-MXFP8 KV Cache support on MRV2, packed TurboQuant KV Cache support, mixed-quant SparseFlashMLA integration, and CANN attention optimizations. Added FP8 Lightning Indexer cache support for CANN KeyPool.

- **KV Cache Pool and Mooncake:** Enhanced layerwise KV Cache transfer, SSD prefetching, offloading, and Mooncake integration, including GLM-5.3-Flash layerwise KV transfer and improved distributed KV Cache management.

- **Performance and Communication:** Optimized MoE execution, expert parallel communication, GDN metadata construction, embedding token exchange, Qwen PLE prefill, sparse attention kernels, and GLM recurrent-state processing.

- **Reliability and Stability:** Fixed issues involving speculative decoding correctness, MRV2 KV Cache initialization and memory accounting, Mooncake synchronization and P/D transfers, PCP/DCP cache layouts, EPLB communication, quantization correctness, and kernel compilation.

For detailed merged features and bug fixes, see the [v0.32.0rc1 Release Checklist](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19867).


## Supported Product Scope
| Model | Hardware supported in this release | Release scope |
|-------|------------------------------------|---------------|
| DeepSeek V4.1 | Atlas 800I A3, Atlas 800I A2 | W8A8 serving; Model Runner V2 execution, TurboQuant INT4 KV cache, torch.compile, P/D deployment |
| GLM-5.3 | Atlas 800I A3 (128GB x 8), Atlas 800I A2 | W8A8C8 multi-node serving; sparse SFA C8 packed KV cache, speculative decoding (DSpark) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | Atlas 800I A3 (128GB x 8), Atlas 800I A2 | W8A8 on A3/A2; P/D disaggregation and KV Cache Pool deployment |
| Qwen3.8-27B | Atlas 800I A3, Atlas 800I A2, Atlas 300I DUO (W8A8-310P) | BF16 and W8A8; hybrid linear-attention serving with non-contiguous KV cache |

**Note:** A merged feature PR does not automatically imply release-level support for every hardware or deployment configuration.

## Environment and Dependencies
- vLLM: v0.30.0
- CANN: 9.2.0
- Ascend HDK: 26.0.RC1
- PyTorch / torch_npu: 2.10.0 / 2.10.0.post4
- Triton Ascend: 3.2.2
- mooncake-transfer-engine-npu: 0.3.11.post1
- flash-linear-attention-npu: v26.9.1-beta2
- ray: >= 2.47.1, <= 2.48.0
- Python: 3.12 (release image base)

## How to Test

Once the v0.32.0rc1 artifacts are published, the release candidate can be tested using one of the following methods.

### Docker

```bash
docker pull quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1
```

### pip

```bash
pip install vllm-ascend==v0.32.0rc1
```

### Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend.git
cd vllm-ascend
git checkout v0.32.0rc1
pip install -e .
```

**Note:** These commands are intended for use after the corresponding tag, wheel, and container images become available. Artifact availability has not yet been confirmed.

Please refer to the versioned model deployment guides and release test report for validated configurations.

## Feedback Guidelines

We welcome community feedback on the v0.32.0rc1 release candidate, particularly in the following areas:

- **Model Compatibility:** Model loading, accuracy, inference correctness, and hardware compatibility.
- **Model Runner V2:** Startup failures, graph capture issues, KV Cache initialization, and runner-specific regressions.
- **Speculative Decoding:** Draft-model execution, MTP, DSpark, acceptance behavior, and verification correctness.
- **Context Parallelism:** PCP/DCP correctness, distributed execution, graph compatibility, and long-context serving.
- **KV Cache Management:** KV Cache Pool, Mooncake, P/D disaggregation, layerwise transfers, prefetching, and offloading.
- **Performance:** Throughput, TTFT, TPOT, memory usage, and regressions compared with previous releases.
- **Distributed Inference:** TP, DP, EP, PP, EPLB, and multi-node communication.
- **Documentation:** Missing deployment instructions, incorrect configuration examples, or unsupported combinations.

Please include the following information when reporting an issue:

```text
- vLLM Ascend version:
- Upstream vLLM version:
- CANN version:
- HDK version and Ascend product:
- PyTorch / torch-npu version:
- Triton Ascend version:
- Hardware and node count:
- Model checkpoint and quantization:
- Model Runner version:
- TP / DP / EP / PP / PCP / DCP configuration:
- Speculative decoding configuration (if applicable):
- KV Cache / Mooncake configuration (if applicable):
- Serving command and workload:
- Steps to reproduce:
- Expected behavior:
- Actual behavior:
- Relevant logs:
- Benchmark or accuracy results (if applicable):
```

## Timeline

- **RC Release Date:** 2026/11/10
- **Next Release Decision:** TBD, based on the release test report and community feedback.

## Related Links

- **Release Checklist:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19867
- **Release Notes:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/docs/source/user_guide/release_notes.md
- **Documentation:** https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/
- **Previous Releases:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/releases

Thank you for testing vLLM Ascend v0.32.0rc1 and helping us improve its stability, compatibility, and performance.

issues.title: [RFC]: Add DSpark speculative decoding support for DeepSeek-V4
issues.body:
### Motivation.

### Motivation.
DeepSeek released DSpark speculative decoding for DeepSeek-V4, with official checkpoints:
- https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark
- https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark
DeepSeek reports **60–85%** faster per-user generation vs MTP-1 at matched throughput (Flash).
vllm-ascend already supports V4 + MTP, but DSpark is not yet a stable spec-decode method. Draft work exists in [#11066](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/11066).
References:
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSpec
- Upstream: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46910


### Proposed Change.

Add DSpark support for DeepSeek-V4 on Ascend:
1. Load official `*-DSpark` checkpoints (Markov head + confidence head).
2. Implement `AscendDsparkProposer` (propose → dynamic verify → reject sample).
3. Expose via `--speculative-config` (prefer `method: "dspark"`, or extend existing MTP path).


### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

_No response_

issues.title: [RFC]: RL Roadmap Q4 2026
issues.body:
### Motivation.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is now a first-class workload for vLLM Ascend. Frameworks such as verl, slime, and vime keep a rollout engine alive for an entire training job and drive it through a lifecycle that ordinary serving never exercises:

- `sleep(level)` / `wake_up(tags)` to hand NPU memory back to a colocated trainer, then take it back;
- `pause_generation(mode)` / `resume_generation()` to stop scheduling while weights change;
- `init_weight_transfer_engine` / `start_weight_update` / `update_weights` / `finish_weight_update` to reload weights in place over HCCL or NPU IPC;
- routed-expert capture (`--enable-return-routed-experts`) and replay so that the trainer reuses the routing decisions produced by inference;
- batch-invariant execution and reproducible logprobs so that training and inference agree.

Every one of these paths is cross-cutting: it touches the worker, the model runner, the memory allocator, ACL graph capture, HCCL, the KV connectors, and every model, quantization, and attention implementation. That is why the same class of defect keeps reappearing. A tensor is silently discarded by sleep. A derived weight is not refreshed after reload. An ACL graph replays with storage that was replaced. A test passes because it only asserts that the API returned successfully.

During Q3 the community wrote three open RFCs that describe the contracts we need:

- **#16558** - Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend.
- **#16322** - Make live weight updates transactional and graph-safe.
- **#12073** - RL test case upgrade.

Those RFCs are the technical core of this roadmap. This issue is the Q4 2026 delivery plan that connects them, adds the replay and code-refactoring workstreams, and lists the RFCs and pull requests that are already in flight so that contributors can see where each item stands and what is still missing.

The roadmap exists because the work is larger than any single PR series, because several items block each other (an allocation boundary must land before owner hooks can be validated; capture layouts must land before topology tests are meaningful), and because we want reviewers to be able to judge each PR against a stated contract instead of against the absence of an immediate failure.

#### Scope of Q4 2026

Five workstreams:

1. **Sleep mode correctness** - tensor ownership and recovery across sleep/wake, including extra cleanup and ACL graph.
2. **Live weight update correctness** - one transactional reload contract for HCCL, NPU IPC, and future backends.
3. **RL test case upgrade** - lifecycle-oriented tests that fail when behavior is wrong, not when an API is merely reachable.
4. **Replay feature enhancement** - Router Replay (R3) capture/replay correctness across topologies and scheduling modes, plus related consistency features.
5. **RL code refactoring** - Worker interface refactor, HCCL weight-update inheritance from the upstream engine, and CaMemAllocator inheritance from the upstream allocator.

#### Status snapshot at filing

| # | Workstream | Tracking RFC | Design state | Q4 outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Sleep mode | #16558 | Ownership contract proposed; phased migration in the RFC | No persistent non-KV tensor is discarded silently by either level, and every releasable buffer is released or documented with a measured size |
| 2 | Weight update | #16322 | Transaction contract proposed; Phase 0 largely landed | HCCL and IPC execute one transaction; derived state is graph-stable |
| 3 | RL tests | #12073 | Test tree designed; partial implementation | PR-gating lifecycle subset plus a nightly matrix |
| 4 | Replay | this issue (no dedicated RFC yet) | Upstream capture-layout contract in review | Topology-complete R3 capture/replay; indexer replay scoped upstream |
| 5 | Refactoring | #18920 (Worker), this issue (transfer, allocator) | Scoped; first pieces merged | Thin adapters over the upstream Worker, NCCL engine, and CuMem allocator |

The RFC/PR lists below were collected from GitHub at filing time and will drift. The tracking RFC remains the source of truth for design detail; this issue tracks delivery.

#### Principles

1. **Upstream first.** Extend the upstream vLLM contract or contribute a hook upstream before adding another Ascend-specific exception. Inherit orchestration; own device mechanisms.
2. **One contract per lifecycle.** Sleep/wake owns memory reclamation. Weight update owns representation. Capture owns logical expert IDs. A feature may not repair a failure that belongs to another lifecycle.
3. **Fail closed.** If a post-capture representation change cannot preserve the storage an ACL graph captured, raise an actionable error instead of silently replacing it.
4. **Tests must be able to fail.** Assert physical memory, `data_ptr()` stability, and output/logprob equality against a fresh cold load. A test that only checks a return code is not coverage.
5. **Measure, do not assume.** Reclaimed memory, wake latency, update throughput, and capture overhead are reported in the PR that changes them.

#### Non-goals

- New RL algorithms, trainer-side changes, or wire-protocol redesign.
- Guaranteeing arbitrary structural model changes during a live update.
- Preserving active-request KV contents across sleep.
- Automatic level-2 parameter reload; the caller-driven reload/update sequence is unchanged.
- Feature parity for Model Runner V1 beyond keeping it startable while it is deprecated (#18202).

---

### Proposed Change.

Each workstream below states the problem, the Q4 deliverables, the existing RFCs and PRs, and the exit criteria. Deliverables are checkboxes so that progress is visible in the issue; a box may only be checked when the change is merged and the stated test exists.

#### 1. Sleep mode correctness

**Problem.** `CaMemAllocator` tags an allocation according to the active pool. `Worker.initialize_from_config()` enters `use_memory_pool(tag="kv_cache")` around the entire `model_runner.initialize_kv_cache()` call, so attention-backend metadata, input-batch state, speculative state, connector registration, sparse-KV/KVPP runtime state, and graph metadata are all created in a discardable scope. At level 1 those allocations are released; at level 2 they are discarded together with the weights. On wake, storage is recreated at the same virtual address, so pointers stay valid while contents do not. An ACL graph can therefore replay with a valid pointer to an erased scale, sentinel, or device pointer table, which surfaces as accuracy loss, a wrong routing decision, or a hang.

**Q4 deliverables.**

Failure visibility (P0)

- [ ] Land the deterministic remap-poison helper: in a fresh subprocess, wrap the NPU remap operation and fill every newly mapped allocation with a recognizable nonzero pattern before the normal host backup is restored.
- [ ] Allocator contract test: allocate a host-backed weight, a KV tensor, and unrelated metadata in a `kv_cache` scope; assert stable addresses, restored weights, and lost KV/metadata contents.
- [ ] Level-2 ownership classification test: parameter, non-persistent registered buffer, and plain tensor attribute; after a poisoned wake and a simulated reload only the first two may recover.
- [ ] One ACL-graph reproducer that captures a graph using a nonzero persistent scale created in the KV scope and fails under the current broad scope.
- [ ] Publish the tensor-ownership inventory (owner, allocation tag, recovery class, first post-wake reader, graph-capture status, test coverage) for MRV1, MRV2, and 310P. The inventory is the acceptance checklist for the migration.

Allocation boundary (P1)

- [ ] Split KV initialization into preparation, cache allocation, and binding; only raw cache backing and its shaped views stay inside `use_memory_pool(tag="kv_cache")`.
- [ ] Apply the same boundary to MRV2, and evaluate 310P independently while preserving its unsupported-feature guards.
- [ ] Move attention-backend metadata, input-batch bookkeeping, speculative/state-space state, connector objects and registration metadata, KVPP runtime state, and graph-manager metadata into the binding phase.
- [ ] Add an allocation audit asserting that only cache backing is tagged `kv_cache` in representative configurations.

Owner recovery protocol (P1)

- [ ] Define a runner-owned lifecycle protocol (`post_sleep_wake(discarded_tags)` / `post_weights_reload()`) with an explicit owner registry; do not traverse arbitrary Python objects to discover tensors.
- [ ] Enforce recovery order: allocator mappings and host-backed bytes, registered model buffers, level-2 reload, derived weights, runtime/HCCL/synchronization state, ACL graph recapture, then admit scheduling.
- [ ] Fold the existing `post_kv_cache_wake_up()` compatibility behavior into this lifecycle as upstream compatibility allows.
- [ ] Convert confirmed static tensors to registered non-persistent buffers or host values; document every remaining `sleep_persistent` allocation with owner, size, and rationale.

Extra cleanup and graphs (P1)

- [ ] Require every owner whose resources extra cleanup destroys to declare graph invalidation; recapture before admitting new work.
- [ ] Verify that re-created HCCL metadata and device pointer arrays reference post-wake resources.
- [ ] Run every touched backend path through at least two sleep/wake cycles, not one.

Model-specific sleep regressions (P1, continuous)

- [ ] DeepSeek-V4.1 sleep defects (#18491), RoPE and derived cos/sin caches (#17217, #18986), MoE layout and L2 communication state (#12269, #12651), target/draft-private state (#18624), and KV-pool interaction (#18118) are fixed or explicitly deferred with a tracking issue.

Reclamation completeness (P0, transactional)

**Problem.** Sleep currently releases two CaMem pools and - only when `rl_config.sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` is enabled - the ACL graphs and the HCCL process groups. Everything else the engine allocates stays in the default torch_npu pool, which sleep never touches: on Ascend there is no `workspace`, `runtime` or `cudagraph` pool, no owner registry, and no per-owner release hook. Upstream closed the same gap on GPU in vllm-project/vllm#59055 by tagging each owner (`workspace` vllm-project/vllm#59156, `runtime` vllm-project/vllm#59158, `cudagraph` vllm-project/vllm#59160, DeepEP vllm-project/vllm#59939, allreduce workspace vllm-project/vllm#59360). This deliverable is the Ascend equivalent, and it is a transaction: accounting first, then tags, then release/restore, then verification, with no step skipped and every number measured.

**Measured baseline** (Ascend 910B 64 GiB die, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.14`, one die, vLLM Ascend `b173effde`, torch_npu 2.10.0, CANN 9.1.0, 2026-10-24). "Mine" is device HBM in use minus the pre-initialisation baseline of the same process, so a neighbour's allocations on the die cancel out.

| Configuration | Awake | Level-1 asleep | Freed | Residual | Sleep | Wake |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `--enforce-eager` | 9.277 | 0.529 | 8.748 | **0.529** | 2.31 s | 0.32 s |
| ACL graph (default) | 9.473 | 0.725 | 8.748 | **0.725** | 2.43 s | 0.31 s |
| ACL graph + `sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` | 9.582 | 0.457 | 9.125 | **0.457** | 2.40 s (level 2: 3.54 s) | 4.01 s (level 2: 7.39 s) |

Values in GiB except the latency columns. The ACL-graph residual decomposes as 419.2 MiB of inactive blocks stranded in the `weights` pool, 292.0 MiB of ACL graph memory pool, 24.0 MiB of live default-pool tensors and <= 15 MiB of CANN runtime and stream state; that accounts for 99% of the measured residual. Extra cleanup buys 0.268 GiB (the graph pool and the captured graph workspaces) for a 13x wake-up cost. On this model the largest single releasable item is not a graph at all: it is the weights pool waste, which no configuration releases.

**What stays resident while asleep, and whether it can be released.**

| Resident while asleep | Where it comes from | Measured | Releasable | How |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Inactive blocks inside the `weights` CaMem pool | `CaMemAllocator` cannot `empty_cache` a pluggable pool (`device_allocator/camem.py`, the `TODO` in `use_memory_pool`) | 419.2 MiB of 1586 MiB (26%) | Yes | trim or compact the pool before the CPU backup, or allocate weight-repacking temporaries in a separate discardable pool |
| ACL graph memory pool | `Platform._global_graph_pool`, `ACLGraphWrapper.graph_pool` (`compilation/acl_graph.py:117`) | 292.0 MiB reserved, 0 active | Yes | drop the handle on sleep and recapture on wake; today only extra cleanup releases it, and it never drops the platform handle |
| Recorded graph op workspaces (`capture_resources`, e.g. `npu_fused_infer_attention_score.workspace`) and `_graph_params.workspaces` | `compilation/acl_graph.py`, `compilation/updatable_graph.py` | 1.43 GiB of references over 150 entries; 274 MiB actually returned | Yes | already cleared by `AclGraphSleepWakeupManager.sleep()`; report it and release the pool behind it |
| HCCL process groups (7 at TP=1) | `HcclSleepWakeupManager` | ~0 MiB returned to the driver at TP=1 | Partly | destroy/restore exists; must be measured at TP8/EP8, where the equivalent NCCL buffers are 1.26-1.64 GiB/GPU upstream |
| Attention and context-parallel scratch sized by tokens x hidden | `attention/dsa_v1.py:1691-1719` (`_oproj_send_buf`, `_oproj_recv_buf`, `_oproj_rs_out_buf`), `attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py:648` and `:921`, `attention/context_parallel/dsa_cp.py:2244`, `attention/dsa_v41.py:601-605` | not allocated on the 0.6B dense path | Yes | `workspace` pool |
| MoE dispatch and combine buffers, expert counters, EPLB tables | `ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py:276`, `ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py`, `ops/fused_moe/eplb.py` | not measured yet (needs a MoE reference configuration) | Yes for scratch, no for state | split `workspace` and `runtime` |
| Speculative-decoding draft state (MTP/EAGLE/DFlash) | `worker/v2/spec_decode/*` | not measured yet | Yes | `runtime` pool |
| Weight-transfer packed buffers | `distributed/weight_transfer/packed_tensor.py` (`DEFAULT_PACKED_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES = 1 GiB`, `DEFAULT_PACKED_NUM_BUFFERS = 2`) | 2 GiB HCCL or 1 GiB NPU IPC per rank while a transfer is in flight | Yes | free them at `finish_weight_update`, or tag them `workspace` |
| Sparse-KV offload and KVPP runtime arenas | `distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/.../sparse_kv_offload_manager.py` | feature dependent | Yes | owner hook |
| `sleep_persistent` tag (DSA Hadamard, ...) | `device_allocator/camem.py` | small, by design | No | document the size and rationale per allocation |
| CANN runtime, streams, kernel modules | driver | <= 15 MiB once the weights-pool waste is excluded | No | - |

**The transaction.**

- [ ] T0 - Accounting before anything else: a `sleep_memory_report()` worker RPC that reports, at every stage, device free/used, per-tag CaMem bytes, per-pool reserved/active/inactive, the graph-pool reservation, the HCCL communicator count, and the delta attributed to the last release step. Today `SleepWakeupManager.sleep()` logs "released HCCL and attention workspace memory: 0.000 GiB" in every measured run, because it samples free memory around its own calls, before the allocator releases the cache; nothing below is "done" without a number from T0.
- [ ] T1 - Tags: add `workspace`, `runtime` and `cudagraph` pools matching vllm-project/vllm#59156, #59158 and #59160, and move the owners in the table above into them, one owner per PR.
- [ ] T2 - Release and restore: give every tagged owner an explicit discard-versus-backup policy and a restore path; keep `sleep_persistent` only for state that cannot be rebuilt.
- [ ] T3 - Verification per phase: bit-exact wake, ten sleep/wake cycles with a flat device-memory slope, a stated host RAM budget for the CPU backup, and sleep/wake latency before and after.
- [ ] T4 - Fail closed: if a live ACL graph references storage that a release step discarded, raise instead of replaying stale storage, and record the invalidation in the owner registry.

**Exit criteria for the transaction.**

- Every row of the resident table is either released or documented non-releasable with a measured size.
- Residual asleep memory is reported for the dense one-card reference above, a TP8/EP8 MoE reference, and a two-card configuration, and is non-increasing after each phase.
- Wake-up latency for the default (no extra cleanup) path does not regress by more than 2x.
- A PR-gating test fails when a new allocation site lands outside a tagged pool.

**Existing RFCs and PRs.**

- #16558 - `[RFC] Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend` (open). Upstream counterpart: vllm-project/vllm#53343.
- vllm-project/vllm#59055 - `[RFC]: Release all releasable GPU memory in sleep mode` (upstream tracking issue; its per-owner release PRs - #59156 workspace, #59158 runtime, #59160 cudagraph, #59939 DeepEP, #59360 allreduce workspace - are what this deliverable mirrors on Ascend).
- #18838 - `[bugfix] preserve configured parameters across level-2 sleep on Ascend` (merged).
- #16725 - `[BugFix][Sleep Mode] Register level-2 runtime tensors as non-persistent buffers` (merged).
- #13352 - `[BugFix] Restore MoE and DSA control buffers after level-2 wake` (merged).
- #13757 - `[BugFix][Device Allocator] Fix CaMem sleep race with in-flight graph replay` (merged).
- #15340 - `[BugFix][Sleep] Keep a dedicated 1 MiB HCCL lifecycle anchor` (merged).
- #13005 - `[MRV2][Feature] Support sleep-mode` (merged).
- #17666 / #18338 - `Synchronize NPU worker device` in sleep/wake (merged; the second is the v0.30.0 backport).
- #10775 - isolate KV cache from sleep cleanup with a dedicated tag for the Hadamard matrix (merged; see #17025).
- #15702 - `Fix CaMem sleep race with in-flight graph replay` (open follow-up to #13757).
- #12651 - refresh Ascend MoE communication state after L2 wake (open).
- #12269 - `[BugFix][Worker] Fix MoE sleep wakeup layout` (open).
- #17217 - RoPE does not recover after L2 wake (open).
- #18491 - fix sleep mode bug of DeepSeek-V4.1 (open).
- #18624 - preserve selected target and draft-private state across L2 sleep (open).
- #18986 - materialise contiguous RoPE derived cos/sin caches (open; references #16558).
- #18009 - remove the unused sleep-persistent CaMem tag (open).
- #17025 - roll back #10775's Hadamard sleep-persistent tag (open; decide together with #18009).
- #18118 - Mooncake sleep/wake, PD handshake, and prefix-cache reset (open).
- #17850 - restore all-to-all indices after level-2 sleep (closed; the invariant is carried by #16558).

**Exit criteria.**

- No persistent non-KV tensor is allocated in the discardable KV scope without a documented complete-rewrite guarantee.
- Every identified persistent NPU tensor has an owner and a recovery class in the inventory.
- Poisoned level-1 and level-2 tests pass for the selected attention, MoE/HCCL, connector, and ACL-graph paths.
- ACL graph tests prove either in-place restoration or explicit invalidation and recapture.
- Each phase PR reports peak model-load memory, available KV memory, memory freed per level, retained `sleep_persistent` bytes, and wake latency with and without extra cleanup.

#### 2. Live weight update correctness

**Problem.** `process_weights_after_loading()` currently performs checkpoint-to-runtime layout conversion, quantization repacking, derived-weight construction, backend buffer preparation, and memory disposal. A cold-load finalizer is therefore reused as a hot-reload mechanism, although many implementations are not idempotent and allocate new storage. Three invariants are missing:

1. **Representation correctness before load** - every destination is restored to the representation its weight loader expects.
2. **Value freshness after load** - every derived or runtime-only tensor is refreshed from the new source weights in dependency order.
3. **Storage identity before graph replay** - graph-visible persistent tensors and backend bindings still reference the storage ACLGraph captured.

Observed failure patterns include reassignment after `.to()`, `.contiguous()`, `.clone()`, or `npu_format_cast()`; checkpoint/runtime layout mismatch on the next reload; stale `weight_fp32`, `W_UK_T`/`W_UV`, composed projections, scales, and biases; destructive source disposal; non-idempotent work tied to `wake_up()` even though asynchronous RL may never sleep; runtime-owned plain tensors and expert lists that generic layerwise reload cannot see; and different semantics between HCCL and NPU IPC.

**Q4 deliverables.**

Transaction parity (P0)

- [ ] Every backend (HCCL, NPU IPC, future) executes START, LOAD, FINISH with identical semantics, and `model.load_weights(weights)` is called exactly once per chunk on both packed and unpacked paths.
- [ ] Unit tests assert call order, packed/unpacked equivalence, and cleanup when a step raises.
- [ ] No production path repairs checkpoint representation through `wake_up()`.

#### 4. Replay feature enhancement

**Problem.** Router Replay (R3) is what makes MoE RL correct: the trainer replays the expert selections made during inference so that the gradient does not mix different routing decisions for the same tokens. On Ascend the capture path has been carried by a monkey patch, and it has repeatedly produced wrong logical IDs when the physical rows are not simply the tensor shape: TP-local shards, DP-gathered rows, MC2/SP padded shards, hybrid attention, and `AsyncLLM` scheduling all change the row layout or the timing. Replay also interacts with the two other workstreams: weights change between capture and replay, and sleep can discard the buffers that held the capture.

Q4 is therefore about replacing ad-hoc capture with an explicit layout contract, covering the topologies we support, and deciding the scope of indexer replay rather than shipping it half-designed.

**Q4 deliverables.**

Capture layout contract (P0)

- [ ] Adopt the upstream explicit row-layout API for routed-expert capture (vllm-project/vllm#61539, implementation PR vllm-project/vllm#62441) and pass shard sizes, gather groups, and ordered source ranges from the ALLGATHER, ALLTOALL, and MC2/FUSED_MC2 prepare paths.
- [ ] Capture logical expert IDs before expert remapping; keep the legacy router signature when capture is disabled.
- [ ] Delete `patch_routed_experts_capture.py` and its registration, and replace patch-specific tests with layout regression tests (#19561).
- [ ] Report an actionable error, rather than silent wrong output, when capture is requested without the required upstream API or in a rejected PCP/DCP/PP combination.

Topology and scheduling coverage (P1)

- [ ] DP=1 with TP>1: gather top-k across TP ranks and capture logical IDs (#15451, #18502; supersedes #18107).
- [ ] DP>1 with TP; PCP/DCP; hybrid attention (MLA plus DSA, and Mamba/GDN where replay is defined); PP.
- [ ] ACL graph and piecewise replay: replay metadata stays aligned with graph padding (see #18750 and #19034 for the kind of alignment defect to guard against), and no capture buffer aliases an allocation that sleep or a reload discarded.
- [ ] `AsyncLLM`: capture and replay must not block the EngineCore event loop.

#### 5. RL code refactoring

The RL paths accumulated their own copies of upstream flows. Three refactors remove most of that duplication and are prerequisites for the contracts above surviving the next upstream upgrade.

##### 5.1 Worker interface refactor

**Problem.** `NPUWorker` inherits `WorkerBase` and re-implements much of the upstream GPU Worker: `update_config`, `reload_weights`, weight-update orchestration, `execute_model` pipeline-parallel return handling, KV-cache setup, and lifecycle methods. The copies have diverged: upstream forwards `update_config` to the Worker and ModelRunner, Ascend only to the ModelRunner; upstream sets the config context in `reload_weights`; upstream weight updates support DP-indexed payloads, draft-model updates, and cleanup after failure, while Ascend keeps a narrower state machine. Every divergence is a place where an upstream fix does not reach Ascend.

- [ ] For each removed override, prove the Ascend behavior is represented by a hook, backend, or ModelRunner method; add contract tests for `update_config`, `reload_weights`, the weight-update state machine, and `execute_model` return handling.

#### Sequencing and dependencies

| Milestone | Entry gate | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 - visibility and parity | No prerequisite; unblocks M2 | Poison helper, allocator contract test, level-2 classification test, ownership inventory; weight-update transaction parity; consolidated RL harness; capture-layout PR (#19561) reviewable |
| M2 - boundaries and contracts | M1 tests are merged and the inventory is published | KV allocation boundary on MRV1; owner protocol; capture layouts merged; NPUWorker inheritance group 1-2; HCCL engine adapter prototype; weight-update matrix running nightly |
| M3 - completion | M2 contracts are merged | MRV2 boundary and 310P evaluation; full nightly matrix; inheritance and allocator cleanup complete; docs updated; the three RFCs closed or explicitly extended into the next quarter |

Dependencies that can move a milestone:

- **Upstream vLLM.** Capture layouts need vllm-project/vllm#62441; sleep ownership follows vllm-project/vllm#53343; HCCL inheritance needs the upstream transfer-engine API; allocator cleanup needs the upstream `CuMemAllocator` surface. A `main2main` drift that changes these surfaces re-plans the affected milestone.
- **Main2main cadence.** Inheritance only pays off if the supported vLLM commit is updated regularly; otherwise the override list grows again.
- **Hardware.** 310P and A5 validation depends on runner availability; MRV2/310P boundary work is scheduled after the A2 path for that reason.
- **Review bandwidth.** Workstreams 1, 2, and 5 touch the same worker and allocator files; they must be sequenced, not merged in parallel on the same day.

#### Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream API drift (capture layouts, transfer engine, allocator) | Blocks a milestone; forces rework | Track the upstream PRs in this issue; land adapters behind capability checks; fail closed with an actionable message |
| ACL graph recapture cost | Wake or update latency regression | Recapture only when storage changed; measure both paths; keep in-place recovery the default |
| Refactor churn colliding with model bring-up | Merge conflicts, regressions | Stage by interface group; land inheritance behind contract tests; avoid touching unrelated model code |
| Test flakiness on NPU CI | Loss of trust in the matrix | Deterministic poisoning, fixed seeds, quarantine with an owner; no unbounded retries |
| Allocator change affecting serving memory accounting | Under- or over-reclaim in production | Keep serving tests green; report memory metrics in every allocator PR |
| Scope creep (sparse updates, LoRA, indexer replay) | Q4 objectives slip | These are P1/P2; they enter only when the P0 contracts are merged and tested |

#### Alternatives considered

**Continue with per-bug fixes.** Cheaper per fix, but the same defect classes reappear because there is no allocation boundary and no transaction. The Q3 fix list already shows repeated repairs of the same invariants.

**Always recapture ACL graphs after wake or update.** Avoids stale-state failures, but adds latency to every cycle and does not restore eager-mode state. Recapture is the fallback only when in-place recovery is impossible.

**Keep the routed-expert capture monkey patch.** It works for the simplest topology and fails whenever the physical row layout differs from the tensor shape; it also cannot express gather groups. The upstream explicit-layout API is the durable contract.

**Fork the upstream Worker flows.** Keeps Ascend behavior explicit, but every upstream fix must be ported by hand. Inheritance with narrow hooks is the cheaper long-term path, provided the override list is small and reviewed.

- The roadmap is updated monthly; a checkbox is only checked when the change is merged and its test exists.
